{"id": "96:12/q05", "question": "How is the repeated 'Have you seen?' construction parsed?", "turns_on": "Whether raʾayta here requires two objects, what supplies them, and whether an interrogative may answer a condition without fāʾ.", "positions": [{"id": "96:12/q05/p1", "position": "It is cognitive seeing or 'tell me': the first object is the prohibiter or preceding relative clause, while later objects or pronouns are supplied from context.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān argues the first object is the relative clause and the second an interrogative clause, citing 53:33–35, 19:77–78 and 56:58–59; later instances have omitted objects, whose pronouns can denote prohibiter or servant. {"id": "96:13/q12", "question": "When and how was this passage placed in the sura?", "turns_on": "Whether the passage was later occasioned by Abū Jahl and inserted after the opening, or continues the sura's generic description of humanity.", "positions": [{"id": "96:13/q12/p1", "position": "The remainder of the sura came later about Abū Jahl, and the Prophet was directed to place these verses after the opening.", "reasons": "Bint al-Shāṭiʾ reports this as al-Rāzī's first solution; she finds both his accounts possible and takes the sequence as following public preaching and prayer."}, {"id": "96:13/q12/p2", "position": "The generic human in the opening continues into the warnings about transgression and forbidding worship.", "reasons": "Bint al-Shāṭiʾ reports al-Rāzī's second solution: despite creation and blessings, people forget their return, transgress, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety; she considers it possible."}]}
{"id": "96:13/q13", "question": "What theological point is drawn from these acts?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "96:13/q13/p1", "position": "Denial and turning away are acts of human beings, not acts created by God.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī draws this from the threat directed to the disbeliever."}]}
{"id": "96:13/q14", "question": "How broadly does the ban on forbidding prayer apply?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "96:13/q14/p1", "position": "The warning reaches everyone who prohibits prayer itself, but an objection to prayer in a usurped place or disliked time can concern that accompanying circumstance.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī distinguishes prayer as such from a concomitant quality, even though the occasion concerns Abū Jahl."}]}
{"id": "96:13/q15", "question": "Which other verses are linked to the paired acts of denial and turning?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "96:13/q15/p1", "position": "The pair recurs at 92:16, 79:21–22, and 75:32; 92:15–16 also supplies the denier's fate in Hell.", "reasons": "Corpus Coranicum notes the recurring verbs and related discussions at 95:7, 73:11, and 88:23. {"id": "96:13/q16", "question": "What recitation merit is reported for the sura?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "96:13/q16/p1", "position": "A reciter receives reward as though he recited the entire set of shorter suras.", "reasons": "Al-Bayḍāwī transmits this as a prophetic report."}]}
{"id": "96:13/q17", "question": "Can a conditional clause be the second object of أَرَءَيْتَ?", "turns_on": "Whether the second object must itself be interrogative or oath-like, or may be supplied by a conditional and its question together.", "positions": [{"id": "96:13/q17/p1", "position": "No: its second object must be an interrogative or oath clause.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān and other grammarians give this objection; al-Irshād includes an oath-like clause among the permitted forms."}, {"id": "96:13/q17/p2", "position": "Yes: the conditional and following question can together occupy or indicate that second-object position.", "reasons": "Al-Khafājī replies to the objection in al-Ālūsī's account; al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī cite Sībawayh's preferred analysis against the restriction."}]}
